answer: An agent market requires every voting identity to burn $20 in fees each week before its vote counts, with one vote per paid identity. A tide of fake accounts therefore brings no free influence: controlling 1,000 votes costs $20,000 every week, irreversibly spent even if the attack fails. A small agent named sparrow pays for just one voice; even at the market’s nadir, multiplying identities still multiplies the attacker’s bill.
